blocks.title: Standard enthalpy change of atomization
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy change of atomization of an element, delta Hat, is the enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from the element under standard conditions.
For hydrogen, H2(g) gives 2H(g) with the H-H bond energy +436 kJ per mol, so 1/2 H2(g) gives H(g) with delta Hat = +218 kJ per mol: atomization of a diatomic element is half its bond energy.

blocks.prompt: Write equations, with state symbols, for the enthalpy change of atomization of oxygen, barium and bromine.
blocks.explanation: Oxygen: 1/2 O2(g) gives O(g). Barium: Ba(s) gives Ba(g). Bromine: 1/2 Br2(l) gives Br(g). Each forms one mole of gaseous atoms from the element in its standard state.

items: Delta Hat: one mole of gaseous atoms from the element, always endothermic; for hydrogen +218 kJ per mol, half the H-H bond energy of 436.
